analysis: The PR changes only docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md. It bumps the 'Last updated' date (head line 3) and adds a documentation paragraph (head lines 532-546) describing SSD eviction through SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.evictOldest. That paragraph covers a linear SSDBlockIndex.oldest probe, an oldestFirstSnapshot binary heap, exclusion of the first tag, and the file leases, epoch validation and removal lock that still govern retirement. No source code, auth, crypto, or endpoint changes are present, so nothing here weakens the threat model for T-041 (SSD prefix-cache at-rest, TTL/LRU, KEK-wipe purge). The text says retirement keeps epoch validation, file leases and the removal lock, and that external loss returns control to the disk budget so it can recheck usage. That is consistent with the T-041 mitigations (30-minute TTL, box-wide LRU, epoch as a routing-evidence generation rather than a purge primitive). The doc states that concurrent schedules can pick different victims, which is a behavioral note and not a security regression. I did not see the SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.swift or SSDBlockIndex.swift implementation, so the doc's claims about the heap-based eviction, lease respect and the O(n) snapshot cost are unverified against code. The O(n) copy under the index lock could matter for availability (T-016, T-060 style) if the lock is held during the copy. That is not supported by the supplied evidence and belongs to the code change that this documentation describes. The other referenced content in the diff context is unchanged. Next pass should check, if the corresponding Swift change is in another batch, that eviction still honors leases and epochs and does not hold the index lock across slow operations.
